capabilities: Open-vocabulary detection: several category names in one prompt, all instances returned as boxes. Trained with up to 500 boxes per response.
Referring-expression localization of one or more instances using attributes, position, relations or world knowledge. English and Chinese (WeRef-Bench).
Explicit rejection: returns None when the queried target is absent. Trained with reviewed hard negatives and RL reward 1 only for an empty prediction.
Counting (count_box / count_point; the response ends with 'Total number: N.').
Referring / category segmentation and alpha matting via the <OBJ> token and a 9.6M-param pixel decoder (no SAM needed). Masks are full-resolution float maps.
Box-prompted matting/segmentation: a given box is teacher-forced as the response prefix, then <OBJ> decoding. Paper Sec 5.1.7; engine.decode_masks(boxes=...).

Undocumented in README and paper but present in code: task='visual_prompt'. The prompt is 'Locate all similar objects in the image based on the reference boxes: <ref>object 1</ref><box>..</box>', with the reference boxes in the SAME image. No benchmark reported, so quality is UNVERIFIED.
Backends: transformers (sdpa) or vLLM 0.23. Devices: cuda, npu, cpu. Batched generation is available (predict_batch).
prompt_types: Text: a category list (several categories per call, joined as 'a. b. c.')
Text: a free-form referring expression (single phrase, may contain commas). The eval code also has a 'Locate a single instance that best matches...' variant.
Box as input: a pixel xyxy box for box-prompted segmentation/matting, teacher-forced as the response prefix
Box as input: in-image reference boxes for 'find similar objects' (visual_prompt task; code only, not evaluated)
Raw prompt override (prompt=...) and freeform tasks such as grounded captions

NOT supported or documented: a reference image of a specific object from a different image (exemplar or template), multi-image prompts, video, or point-as-input prompts. The package API sends exactly one image per request. The vLLM config allows 10 images, but multi-image use is not documented, trained or evaluated (UNVERIFIED). The model card says it 'currently targets single-turn image perception (video grids are rejected by the pixel decoder)'.

MEASURED BY AUTHORS: only the tutorial latencies above (0.6-1.7 s per call on an unnamed GPU, 4B, transformers). The paper reports no VRAM, latency or throughput figures. Hosted demos run on HF ZeroGPU ("zero-a10g" label in the Space API).

ESTIMATES (mine, not measured): bf16 weights about 9.7 GB for 4B and about 4.9 GB for 2B, plus a 38 MB decoder. Peak VRAM roughly 11-14 GB (4B) and 6-8 GB (2B) at the default limit of 2,025 visual tokens and a context of 8,192 or less, so a 16-24 GB GPU is enough. On CPU the engine forces float32: 4B needs about 19.3 GB of RAM, which does not fit this 16 GB VM; 2B needs about 9.8 GB, which would fit but be slow. That is moot anyway, because the sandbox forbids running it here. Download per GPU box: 19.3 GB for 4B (stored F32) or 4.9 GB for 2B.

Resolution: default max_pixels = 2025*32*32, about 2.07 MP (the paper evaluates at 1,960 tokens or fewer). ego_cam_a 2028x1520 (3.08 MP) would be downscaled about 0.82x linearly; the 1280x800 mono frames (about 1,000 tokens) run near native resolution.

DEPENDENCIES (exact pins in requirements.txt / pyproject): python>=3.10 (README uses a 3.10 conda env), torch==2.11.0, torchvision==0.26.0, transformers==5.12.1, accelerate==1.14.0, huggingface-hub==1.21.0, qwen_vl_utils==0.0.14, safetensors==0.8.0, supervision==0.31.0, pycocotools, scipy, numpy==2.2.6, Pillow==12.2.0. Optional: vllm==0.23.0 + triton==3.6.0, and gradio==6.30.0 for the demo. Install with pip install -e . from the GitHub repo (package wevisone_vl).

No flash-attn is needed (sdpa is the default). The deformable attention is pure PyTorch (F.grid_sample), so there are no custom CUDA ops. from_pretrained is called with trust_remote_code=True, but the HF repos contain no .py files: the architecture is stock transformers Qwen3-VL, and the custom code is the local package. mask_decoder.pt is loaded with weights_only=True. The pinned torch 2.11 / transformers 5.12 stack will likely clash with the FoundationPose environment, so it should run as a separate process or venv.
model.output_format:
The model returns generated text in a Rex-Omni-style format:
- Boxes: <ref>label</ref><box><x0><y0><x1><y1>,<x0><y0><x1><y1></box>, with several labels separated by ', '. Coordinates are integer bins 0-1000, normalized to the input image's width and height and independent of the processor's internal resize. Pixel coordinates are bin/1000*W (or H). One bin is about 2 px on a 2028-px-wide image.
- Points: <point><x><y>,...</point>.
- Absent target: None in the coordinate field.
- Counting appends 'Total number: N.'.
- Segmentation/matting: an <OBJ> token after each box inside <box>. The engine then runs a teacher-forced forward pass and the pixel decoder, giving one float32 sigmoid map per instance, upsampled to the original HxW (an alpha matte; threshold at 0.5 for a binary mask).

Python API: WeVisOneVL(...).predict(image, task, query, prompt=None, reference_boxes=None) returns InferenceResult(response: str, prompt: str, boxes: list of normalized xyxy, filled only for <OBJ> tasks, masks: list[np.ndarray HxW float32], latency_s). Detection boxes have to be parsed from response with evaluation/utils/parser.py (parse_prediction returns {label: [[x0,y0,x1,y1] in pixels]}). save_result writes overlay/alpha/cutout PNGs plus JSON.

The model outputs NO confidence scores; the paper uses F1 for that reason. Token log-probs are not exposed by the package (they could in principle be taken from generate's output_scores; UNVERIFIED).
model.egocentric_or_grayscale_evidence:
Egocentric: the only link is that EgoObjects (Meta's egocentric object dataset, ICCV 2023) is one of 18 public detection sources in the SFT data (paper Table 9; the public detection total is 18.4M / 16.2M / 8.4M samples across S1-S3). The paper reports NO egocentric benchmark (no EgoObjects, Ego4D or EPIC evaluation) and no head-mounted or robot-camera results; 'embodied intelligence' appears only as a motivating application.

Grayscale/mono: NO evidence anywhere in the paper, the model card or the code. There are no grayscale, IR or mono evaluations or augmentations. Every input goes through PIL .convert('RGB'), so a mono frame is replicated to 3 channels, and the decoder's CNN stem also expects RGB. Behaviour on our ego_cam_b/c mono frames is UNVERIFIED.

Relevant measured project fact (STATUS.md): OWLv2 text prompts failed on our mono images, so text grounding on mono is a known risk here. Running it on the ego_cam_a colour frame and carrying boxes or masks into the stereo frame via the extrinsics is the natural path; that is a hypothesis, not tested.
model.instance_vs_category:
Category and language-described instance only, within one image. It can single out a specific instance in the current image when language can describe it (attributes, colour, position, relations; e.g. 'the black and white dog' gives one box). It is trained to answer None when nothing matches. On our classes it is strongest at catching hallucinated absent objects (WeRef Rej 96.4% for 4B, but only 67.4% on public RefCOCOg-Rej and 52.6% on PR-Bench).

It CANNOT take a reference image of a specific object from another image (a scan render, template or exemplar crop). It cannot do CNOS-style instance matching against our mesh renders, and it gives no identity embedding. The code-only 'visual_prompt' task takes reference boxes in the same image and returns 'all similar objects', which is category-like similarity, not identity, and is not evaluated.

Consequence for us (assessment, not measured): it could name and box 'white saucepan', 'lime green dust pan', 'blue cup', 'wooden spoon' and so on from the kit's object names (allowed at inference). It cannot tell the two near-identical bamboo boards apart except by spatial wording, so board identity must still come from our own geometry, size or marker logic. It also cannot tell our specific beige cup from another beige cup in the scene.
limitations: Very new: arXiv v1 and weights released 22 Oct 2026, with no independent reproduction. All baseline numbers are the authors' own runs. WeRef-Bench and WeRefMat are in-house, and the headline rejection rate 96.4 comes from the in-house set; public RefCOCOg-Rej is 67.4 (4B) / 50.2 (2B) and PR-Bench Rej is 52.6 / 37.0.

Detection is reported as F1 (no AP, because there are no confidence scores), so it is not comparable with the AP literature. The only specialist detector baseline is GroundingDINO-T; there is no comparison with SAM3, OWLv2 or GroundingDINO-B/L for detection.

No confidence scores per box: candidates cannot be ranked or thresholded. Our frame-0 seeding currently scores and gates candidates, so its scores would have to come from our own verifiers (size gate, DINOv2 template score, FoundationPose).
Single image per call; no multi-image, video or reference-image prompts. The model card says the pixel decoder rejects video grids. Fine-tuning code has not been released.
No egocentric or grayscale evaluation; inputs are forced to RGB. Mono-camera use is untested, and OWLv2 already failed on our mono frames (measured, STATUS.md).

Default input cap is about 2.07 MP (2,025 visual tokens; trained and evaluated at 1,960 or fewer). The 3.08 MP colour frames are downscaled about 0.82x, which may hurt small or thin objects (spoon) and is UNVERIFIED for our scenes. Box coordinates are quantized to 1/1000 of the image size.

Model card limitations: fine alpha boundaries are sensitive to resolution, severe occlusion, transparency and prompt phrasing; there is no chain-of-thought; single-turn only. Paper limitations: limited general-purpose data may reduce general abilities versus base Qwen3-VL; benchmark prompts are cleaner than real queries. RL used box-only rewards (mask quality was not RL-optimised).

Heavy, exactly pinned new stack (torch 2.11.0, transformers 5.12.1, optional vllm 0.23.0) that likely conflicts with the FoundationPose environment, so a separate process or venv is needed. The 4B checkpoint is stored as F32 (19.3 GB download per rented box); the 2B is 4.9 GB.
Measured compute figures are limited to tutorial latencies on an unnamed GPU; the VRAM figures here are my estimates.

Could not verify: GitHub repo creation date, star count or issue tracker (GitHub API blocked in this session; repo read via git clone and raw files); Figure 3 task-format examples (image only); the training mix for the visual_prompt task (FSC-147 / FSCD-147 exemplar datasets are listed for counting/detection, but the paper never describes visual prompting); how well visual_prompt or multi-image vLLM requests work.

Fit assessment (hypothesis, not measured): most useful as an extra text-grounding or verification term on the ego_cam_a colour frame at frame 0, e.g. to reject wrong-object candidates such as a rack fragment or the wrist watch and to propose boxes for SAM2/FoundationPose. It would not replace the scan-matching detector for instance identity. Falsifying experiment: run 2B and 4B (temperature 0, all kit object names in one detection prompt, plus a per-object referring prompt) on the public-episode frame-0 colour frames that already have labels (tools/det_score.py set: 18 episodes / 72 frames). Then compare per-object correct-box rate and absent-object false positives against the current SAM2 x DINOv2 detector, using public data only. Estimated cost is about one short 24 GB GPU job (under 1 h, roughly $0.5-1 plus the 5-19 GB download); this is an estimate and needs the owner's go-ahead.

candidates.name: WeVisOne-VL 2B / 4B (Tencent WeChat Vision, released 2026-10-22). This is the reference model the others are compared against.
candidates.what: A vision-language model built on Qwen3-VL. It predicts boxes as coordinate tokens, then an <OBJ> token drives a small pixel decoder (about 9.5-9.6M parameters, Deformable-DETR-style, coarse-to-fine) that outputs binary masks or alpha mattes. Tasks: detection, referring expressions, counting, pointing, OCR, referring segmentation and matting. It returns 'None' when the target is absent.
candidates.instance_prompting: NO. The documented API is text only: predict(image, task, query). There are no exemplar or reference-image inputs. The card says 'single-turn image perception', and video grids are rejected by the pixel decoder. The paper uses box-as-prefix input only in its matting evaluation. Multi-image input is undocumented (unverified, even though the Qwen3-VL base supports it).
candidates.key_numbers: From the paper, arXiv 2610.31329. Detection is Mean F1 over IoU 0.5-0.95, not AP. COCO 0-shot: 4B 57.1, 2B 55.2 (LocateAnything-3B 54.7, Rex-Omni-3B 52.9, Qwen3-VL-4B 48.7). LVIS: 55.3 / 53.3 (Rex-Omni 46.9). Dense200: 71.3 (4B). RefCOCOg referring detection F1: 80.8 / 81.8 (4B). Referring segmentation cIoU, 4B: RefCOCO val/testA/testB 81.4/84.5/80.1, RefCOCO+ 76.5/81.1/72.8, RefCOCOg 77.7/77.8. ReasonSeg gIoU 71.2. Rejection of absent objects (Ref-ZOM): 4B 86.0 %, 2B 62.4 % (UniPixel-7B 0.3 %). No COCO mask AP, no comparison with SAM 3, no latency figures.
candidates.licence: Code: Apache-2.0 for Tencent-authored code; third-party parts keep their own licences. Weights: the HF tag on both 2B and 4B says apache-2.0, and the base Qwen3-VL is Apache-2.0. Clean for an Apache release. The README gives no separate weights licence text (minor gap).
candidates.compute: HF safetensors: 2B ≈ 2.44 B params, 4B ≈ 4.83 B. Estimate ≈ 5 / 10 GB VRAM in bf16, so a 24 GB GPU (RTX 3090/4090) is enough. Backends are transformers or vLLM. Speed is not reported. The code is 4 days old.
candidates.fit_for_us: (a) Helps with category confusions (pot vs rack vs watch strap, pot vs lid vs handle) through attribute and referring text plus rejection. It cannot tell the two bamboo boards apart: text gives no instance identity. (b) It is an RGB model with no grayscale evidence, so run it on colour camera a. Colour also fixes the blue/beige cups. (c) Its masks look good (RefCOCO cIoU 81). It is the Apache-clean option for text-to-mask on camera a, but it is not better proven than SAM 3. Worth a cheap bake-off; not the first pick.

candidates.name: SAM 3 / SAM 3.1 (Meta; Nov 2025, ICLR 2026; 3.1 'Object Multiplex' 2026-03-27)
candidates.what: Promptable Concept Segmentation: a short noun phrase and/or image exemplars (boxes, positive or negative) return masks and identities for all matching instances, in images and video. A DETR-style detector with a presence head and a SAM2-style memory tracker share one Perception Encoder backbone. It also takes SAM-2-style points, boxes and masks. SAM 3.1 adds joint multi-object tracking with shared memory.
candidates.instance_prompting: PARTLY. Exemplars must be boxes in the same image. Cross-image exemplars are not supported natively: the maintainer reply in GH issue #426 says 'the concept is bounded with the image itself'; see also #185, #317, #265. Workaround: paste the reference crop and the target side by side on one canvas, put the box on the reference half, and keep detections from the target half. Users: FSS-SAM3 (arXiv 2604.05433, code WongKinYiu/FSS-SAM3, training-free), CG-ICS (arXiv 2606.28149, ECCV 2026), PickNik's MoveIt Pro exemplar node. These benchmarks are category-level few-shot, not instance-level. The prompt is concept-level by design: a positive box on board 1 asks for every board.
candidates.key_numbers: Paper Table 1, zero-shot text. LVIS mask AP 48.5 (DINO-X 38.5, OWLv2* 43.4); LVIS box AP 53.6; COCO box AP 56.4 (DINO-X 56.0, gDino-T 45.7); COCO-O 55.7. SA-Co/Gold instance cgF1 54.1 (human 72.8, OWLv2* 24.6, OWLv2 17.3, gDino-T 3.3, Gemini 2.5 13.0). Table 3, one same-image exemplar, image-only AP+: COCO 76.8 / LVIS 76.0 / ODinW13 82.2 vs T-Rex2 58.5 / 65.8 / 61.8; text+image 78.1 / 78.4 / 81.8. Interactive: +21.6 cgF1 over text-only after 3 exemplar clicks. Video: SA-V test J&F 84.4 vs SAM2.1-L 78.4; MOSEv2 60.3 vs 47.9 (from our notes 03). Correction to docs/research/notes/03-lit-perception.md: '48.5/37.2' is LVIS mask AP / cgF1, not box/mask AP.
candidates.licence: SAM License, custom, not OSI. It covers code and weights. It gives a royalty-free licence to use, copy, distribute and modify, with no non-commercial clause. Conditions: pass on the licence, acknowledge use in published research, trade-control and end-use bans (military, nuclear, espionage, weapons), indemnity, and termination if you bring an IP suit. HF weights are gated by manual approval (facebook/sam3, facebook/sam3.1). Owner action: request access and check our token. STATUS says the token lacked the SAM 3D gate. Whether an Apache-2.0 release of our code may depend on it is our open question 'A1' (notes 03).
candidates.compute: 848 M params (HF 860 M). The paper reports ≈ 30 ms per image with 100+ objects on an H200, and near real time for about 5 objects in video. Needs Python ≥ 3.12, PyTorch ≥ 2.7, CUDA ≥ 12.6. Fits a 24 GB GPU (estimate). The canvas trick roughly doubles backbone cost.
candidates.fit_for_us: Best overall candidate for (a) category confusions and (c) masks. Text prompts like 'white cooking pot', 'pot lid' and 'dish rack' on colour camera a give whole-object instance masks, which addresses the part-versus-whole errors (ep2 pot mask on the lid; eval 1 pot→handle, lid→pot). The presence head cuts hallucinated hits. The video tracker can carry masks through occlusion. It does NOT pick one twin board: same concept. (b) No published grayscale numbers. Exemplars cut from our own mono frames avoid the colour gap (hypothesis).

candidates.name: CAD-Prompted SAM3 (arXiv 2602.20551, Feb 2026; a 2026 instance-level, mesh-prompted detector)
candidates.what: SAM 3 fine-tuned to segment the instances of one specific CAD model. 12 canonical renders of the mesh each go through SAM 3's image encoder, with 25 points sampled inside the render mask. SAM 3's GeometryEncoder turns each view into an exemplar embedding, and the 12 are concatenated as prompt tokens. So cross-image, geometry-conditioned exemplars work after fine-tuning. Training: about 15k Isaac-Sim images with 9k ABC meshes and randomised appearance; half the images contain two or more copies of the same model.
candidates.instance_prompting: YES, from mesh renders, which is our setting (we have scan meshes). Prompting from real reference photos is not documented.
candidates.key_numbers: PQ / F1 / mIoU, no AP. Custom 3D-print set: 0.754 / 0.803 / 0.749 vs best baseline (adapted Matcher) 0.514 / 0.573 / 0.446. T-LESS: 0.317 / 0.371 / 0.327 vs 0.173 PQ. ITODD: PQ 0.536 vs 0.415 for plain SAM 3 exemplar prompting. 0.46 s per object on an RTX 4070. No CNOS, SAM-6D or NIDS-Net comparison. Look-alikes are not evaluated beyond T-LESS.
candidates.licence: Code at github.com/kevinPOI/cad_prompted_sam3. The licence type is not named on the page (unverified); the code is built on heyoeyo/muggled_sam. It needs the gated SAM 3 weights (SAM License). The fine-tuned checkpoint is on Google Drive. The author calls it a 'messy work-in-progress'. Renders need Blender 5.0.
candidates.compute: Laptop-class GPU (RTX 4070) for inference. Training cost is not reported.
candidates.fit_for_us: The most direct 2026 upgrade of our CNOS-style step (SAM2 automatic proposals × DINOv2 vs grey renders). It conditions on geometry and ignores appearance, so it should transfer to mono frames (hypothesis). But geometry-only conditioning cannot tell the two boards apart either: our board meshes lack the slots, so they are geometrically alike (work log 2026-10-24). Research-grade code.

candidates.name: MUSE and the BOP-H3 leaders (model-based 2D detection of unseen objects; BOP 2025)
candidates.what: MUSE (arXiv 2510.17866) is a training-free CNOS successor. Grounding DINO (Swin-B, prompt 'items') plus SAM2-L give proposals. DINOv2-L class and patch (GeM) embeddings are compared with multi-view mesh templates, using von Mises-Fisher view weighting and an uncertainty-aware objectness prior. Its abstract says it ranked first on the BOP 2025 Classic-Core, H3 and Industrial 2D-detection tracks. The current BOP-H3 leader, 3PT-Detection (Nov 2025), is unpublished and has no code.
candidates.instance_prompting: YES, from the object mesh (rendered templates). This is exactly our CNOS-style setup.
candidates.key_numbers: BOP-H3 2D detection AP, live leaderboard fetched 2026-10-26: 3PT-Detection 0.548 (HOT3D 0.484) at 6.6 s/img; MUSE 0.418 (HOT3D 0.438, HOPEv2 0.460, HANDAL 0.357) at 0.92 s on an RTX 4090; CNOS-FastSAM 0.303 (HOT3D 0.350). Classic-Core: MUSE 0.533; CLON (RGB-D, Jun 2026) 0.552; NIDS-Net 0.469. MUSE ablations: patch+class fusion +0.018 APcore; objectness prior +0.028. candidates.licence: No official code or licence found (unverified).
candidates.fit_for_us: Watch-list only until code and weights are confirmed.

alts.takeaway:
WeVisOne-VL is worth one cheap test, but it is not the best fix for our detection problem, and it does not take a picture of the object as a prompt. It is text only: it finds objects from a description and returns masks. It has two real strengths. Its licence is clean (code and weights Apache-2.0), and it is good at saying "not present" (86 % rejection on Ref-ZOM for the 4B model). It was released 4 days ago, reports no speed figures, and has never been compared with SAM 3.

Our measured state, from the repo: the frame-0 detection rule picks the right mask for 93 of 116 labelled public instances (24/29 at frame 0). The misses split into three kinds:
- **Different objects that look alike:** the pot mask spills onto the lid (ep2); on eval 1 our own frame-0 output (no ground truth) gives the pot to its handle and the lid to the whole pot; eval 30's sweeper went to a wrist blob (fixed by the Grounding DINO re-proposal).
- **Colour lost in grayscale:** in ep11 the blue cup took the beige cup's proposal, and the beige cup went to the person's lap.
- **True twins:** the two boards are swapped in ep23.

**(a) Choosing the right instance among look-alikes**
- **Different objects that look alike** (white pot vs rack vs watch strap, pot vs lid vs handle): SAM 3 is the best fix, run with text prompts on colour camera a. It returns whole-object masks and leads clearly on concept segmentation (SA-Co/Gold 54.1 vs OWLv2 17.3 and Grounding DINO tiny 3.3). WeVisOne-VL-4B is the Apache-clean second choice. Keep our reach, size, table and FoundationPose depth checks on top.
- **True twins** (the two near-identical bamboo boards): no model in this survey separates them.
  - SAM 3 works at the level of a concept, so a box on board 1 asks for every board.
  - WALDO (Aug 2026) measured exemplar matching at chance for picking a specific instance (0.19 vs a 0.19 floor).
  - Mesh-prompted methods (CAD-Prompted SAM3, MUSE) see the same geometry for both boards, because our board meshes lack the slots.
  - The fix has to come from geometry: board meshes with the slots, compared against the stereo depth. The mocap marker layout is another identity cue (note 17), and so is agreement across several frames.
  - This is a hypothesis. To falsify it, run SAM 3 on public ep23 frame 0 with a board-1 crop pasted beside the frame (the "canvas" workaround) and check whether its score separates the two boards by more than about 0.1.
- **Blue vs beige cup:** this is a colour problem, covered under (b).

**(b) Mono grayscale frames.** The best fix is not a model. Detect on colour camera a and carry the masks into the rectified mono frame through stereo depth and the camera-a to b/c extrinsics. We already do this for Grounding DINO boxes (boxes_in_a, A_OFFSET=1). This restores colour (blue vs beige cup) and puts every model back on the RGB data it was trained on. If a model must run on mono frames directly:
- **SAM 2.1 or SAM 3**, prompted with crops cut from the same mono stream (the canvas trick), avoids the colour gap. This is a hypothesis; I found no grayscale benchmark for any of these models.
- **MUSE-style mesh matching** is the closest public evidence. On HOT3D, an egocentric set with monochrome streams, MUSE scores 0.438 AP vs CNOS 0.350, and the unpublished leader 3PT-Detection scores 0.484. Whether the HOT3D 2D test images are mono is unverified.
- **Avoid OWLv2 on grayscale:** our own measurement on 2026-10-13 was negative.

**(c) Masks good enough to seed 6-DoF tracking**
- **SAM 3:** instance masks (LVIS mask AP 48.5 zero-shot vs DINO-X 38.5), plus a video tracker for occlusions. The licence is Meta's custom SAM License with gated weights, so the owner needs to request access and decide whether it fits the Apache release.
- **Fully Apache option:** WeVisOne-VL masks (RefCOCO cIoU 81.4), or box prompts into SAM 2.1 on the mono frame. The box-only models (Qwen3-VL, Rex-Omni, LocateAnything, Florence-2) all need SAM for masks.

**Excluded:**
- Licence: Rex-Omni and T-Rex2 (IDEA non-commercial), LocateAnything (NVIDIA non-commercial), YOLOE (AGPL).
- Hosted API only, no weights (not reproducible): Grounding DINO 1.5/1.6, DINO-X, T-Rex2.
- Too weak: Florence-2 and OWLv2. OWLv2 already failed on our grayscale frames.

**Suggested experiment** (needs the owner's go-ahead; this VM's sandbox does not allow running the model code here):
- **What:** one GPU box, a single 24 GB card, about 1 hour. Estimate about $1-3, not quoted.
- **Contenders:** SAM 3 (text, plus canvas exemplar) and WeVisOne-VL-4B (text), both on camera a.
- **How:** use the existing public frame dumps. Replay each as a replacement for the Grounding DINO tiny term, or as extra proposals, with tools/det_replay.py.
- **Acceptance, fixed in advance:** more than 93/116 correct with no instance lost.
- **Also report:** ep11, ep23 and ep2 separately, and the board score margin.
- **Integrity:** public episodes only; eval episodes are not touched for tuning.

One correction for docs/research/notes/03-lit-perception.md: the SAM 3 figures "48.5/37.2" are LVIS mask AP and a concept-F1 score (cgF1), not box and mask AP. SAM 3's LVIS box AP is 53.6. Still unverified: MUSE code availability, the cad_prompted_sam3 licence, whether T-Rex-Omni and PET-DINO weights are released, how well Qwen3-VL picks an instance from two images, and any model's accuracy on grayscale.

Prompt types: category list ('a. b. c.'), free-form referring phrase (plus a 'Locate a single instance...' eval variant), a pixel xyxy box for box-prompted seg/matting teacher-forced as the response prefix, in-image reference boxes (visual_prompt, code only, not evaluated), raw prompt / freeform. checks.evidence: Almost all of this checks out. Only the box-input detail is wrong. Confirmed: prompts.py has detection = "Locate all the instances that match the following description: " + ". ".join(labels) + "." and a docstring saying "A referring expression remains a single phrase even when it contains commas." evaluation/utils/prompt_builder.py has "Locate a single instance that best matches the following description: {phrase}". For visual_prompt the docstring says "Reference boxes are pixel-space [x1, y1, x2, y2]" and the prompt is "Locate all similar objects in the image based on the reference boxes". visual_prompt is not mentioned in the README, the eval scripts or the paper; it is reachable only through predict() and the CLI flag --reference-boxes. predict(prompt=...) overrides the template, and the demo has caption presets such as "describe the image with bounding boxes in detail". engine._inputs passes `images=[image]` (one image per request), and vLLM uses `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 10, "video": 10}`. The card says "currently targets single-turn image perception (video grids are rejected by the pixel decoder)". No task takes a point as input; 'point' is pointing output. Paper: "return None when the target is absent". Tutorial: 'the black and white dog' gives one box. Table 3 gives 4B Rej 96.4 (WeRef), 67.4 (RefCOCOg-Rej) and 52.6 (PR-Bench). WRONG: box-prompted matting does not take a pixel xyxy box as a response prefix. In evaluation/inference_matting.py, tight_alpha_box returns a "Normalized xyxy box". box_response() writes the whole response as `<ref>{expression}</ref><box>{coords}<OBJ></box>` with coords = round(v*1000), and engine.decode_masks(image, prompt, response, boxes=...) teacher-forces it; its docstring says "`boxes` (normalized xyxy)". The model generates no continuation, and the user prompt is still the text template with an expression. This path cannot be reached from predict() or the CLI, only from decode_masks. The pixel-xyxy convention belongs to visual_prompt. Other caveats: 'on our classes' is not measured, because the Rej figures are benchmark results. The paper says each <OBJ> hidden state 'serves as a latent representation of the corresponding instance', but it is internal (not returned by the API) and not trained for identity. The 'no identity embedding' point holds in practice.

Prompts use det_rules.prompt(name) (underscores to spaces, trailing digits dropped). Decoding is greedy, the backend is transformers with sdpa, max_pixels is the default 2025*32*32, and the code is pinned to WeVisOne commit 9a6bcd8 and the HF shas 798ffc7 (2B) and 4a7bed9 (4B).

verdict.summary: WeVisOne-VL is worth one small test, but it should not be built into the pipeline yet. It is a new (22 Oct 2026) Tencent model that finds objects from text and can answer 'not there'. Its code and weights are Apache-2.0, so it is safe for our release. The authors benchmark it directly against the exact helper model our detector uses now, Grounding DINO tiny. It wins clearly on long-tail objects (LVIS mean F1 55.3 vs 38.8), on finding a described object (RefCOCOg 80.8 vs 45.9) and on refusing absent ones (67 % vs 0 %). On COCO it is about even (57.1 vs 56.6). All of these are the authors' own numbers on a 4-day-old model, with no independent reproduction. It cannot fix our hardest detection problems. It cannot tell the two identical bamboo boards apart, it has no evidence on our grayscale stereo frames, it cannot take a picture of our specific object as a prompt, and it gives no confidence scores. Detection is also no longer our main loss. On public data our detector now gets 97 of 116 labelled objects right (the summary's 93 is out of date), and the remaining frame-0 misses are the twin boards plus the pot and lid on ep2. Most of the remaining leaderboard gap is spoon pose and policies that fail to follow the reference. My recommendation is a pre-registered public-only test (about $1-1.5, under an hour of GPU, decision within a day). It swaps WeVisOne in for Grounding DINO in our existing offline replay and scores against the public labels. Adopt only if it reaches at least 99 of 116 with nothing lost, at an acceptable speed; otherwise drop it and keep the time for the bigger levers before the 4 November freeze.
